title: The Untold Story Behind the Sons of Sceva Trying to Use Jesus’ Name
paragraphs: The Untold Story Behind the Sons of Sceva Trying to Use Jesus’ Name
There are people who say the name of Jesus with tears in their eyes.
And there are people who say it like a password.

Most believers know the story of the Sons of Sceva from a few verses buried inside Acts 19, but very few understand how terrifying, heartbreaking, prophetic, and painfully relevant this story truly is.
Because this was never just about seven Jewish exorcists.
This was about people trying to borrow intimacy with God that they never pursued themselves.
This was about using the name of Jesus without surrendering to the authority of Jesus.
This was about spiritual performance without relationship.
A generation is still doing it.
The room gets quiet whenever heaven exposes counterfeit spirituality.
Acts 19 does not read like a comfortable church story.
It reads like a warning siren.

The Apostle Paul had arrived in Ephesus, one of the darkest spiritual centers in the ancient world. Ephesus was consumed with idol worship, occult practices, magical arts, temple prostitution, and demonic activity. The city was famous for the Temple of Artemis, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. Sorcery was not hidden there.

“God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul: so that from his body were brought unto the sick handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out of them.”
The authority of Christ was publicly destroying darkness.
And that is where the story becomes disturbing.
Because some men saw the power...
“Then certain of the vagabond Jews, exorcists, took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus.”
The phrase “took upon them” comes from the Greek phrase:
“To attempt arrogantly.” “To put one’s hand to something presumptuously.” “To undertake without authorization.”
They were not moving in faith.
They were experimenting with holy things.
And that is far more common today than many Christians want to admit.
People wear crosses but refuse surrender.
People use Christian language while living in hidden rebellion.
People know worship songs but do not know God.
There are pulpits full of charisma without consecration.
Content creators chasing influence without prayer.
Church culture that knows branding better than brokenness.
many people are terrified that they have learned how to sound spiritual without actually being transformed.
The Sons of Sceva were not atheists.
That is what makes this story terrifying.
Their father, Sceva, is described in Greek as:
Whether this title was official or self-appointed is debated among scholars, but the point remains:
These men were deeply connected to religious culture.
Yet demons still recognized they lacked authority.
Religion without relationship has always been powerless.
The seven sons approached a demonized man and declared:
“We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.”
And hell immediately recognized the difference.
Acts 19:15 records one of the most chilling verses in the New Testament:
“And the evil spirit answered and said, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?”
The Greek language here is incredibly revealing.
For “Jesus I know,” the demon uses:
For “Paul I know,” the Greek is:
But heaven had no record of surrendered intimacy from these men.
Acts 19:16 says the demonized man leaped on them, overpowered them, and they fled naked and wounded.
Because counterfeit spirituality is eventually exposed.
You can fake power before people.
You cannot fake authority before hell.
That sentence alone should shake modern Christianity.
But demons do not respond to branding.
Spiritual authority is born from surrender, obedience, prayer, holiness, intimacy, repentance, and submission to Christ.
There are people exhausted right now because they have been trying to use the language of faith while secretly starving spiritually.
They know how to post about Jesus.
But they do not spend time with Him.
They know how to quote verses.
And eventually, the soul begins collapsing under the weight of pretending.
This is why the story matters.
Not because God wanted to humiliate people.
But because Jesus refuses to be used like a magical incantation.

In Jewish culture during the first century, many itinerant exorcists believed certain names carried supernatural force. Ancient magical papyri from the Greco-Roman world reveal people invoking names of deities, angels, and spiritual beings as formulas for power.
The Sons of Sceva treated Jesus like one more formula.
But Jesus is not a spell.
His name is connected to His person.
“Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name.”
The Greek word for “name” here is:
But in biblical thought, a name represented identity, character, authority, and essence.
To invoke the name of Jesus while rejecting the Lordship of Jesus is spiritual contradiction.
And this is where many people feel pierced.
Because there are countless individuals sitting in churches while secretly feeling disconnected from God.
Some are performing Christianity because they fear disappointing people.
Some are trying to inherit faith from parents.
Some are living on old encounters.
Some know church language but have never fully surrendered their lives to Christ.
And beneath all the noise is a terrifying question:
“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?”
The Greek word for “knew” is again:
That verse should destroy every illusion that outward spiritual activity automatically equals inward transformation.
God has never been impressed with performance detached from surrender.
The story does not end in hopelessness.
Because the aftermath of Acts 19 became one of the greatest revivals in Ephesus.
Those practicing occult arts burned their books.
Acts 19:19 says the value of the burned books was fifty thousand pieces of silver.
Real encounters with the holiness of God always expose what cannot remain.
The Greek word used for confessed in Acts 19:18 is:
“To openly acknowledge.” “To confess fully.” “To admit without concealment.”
Revival began when people stopped hiding.
And maybe that is the real reason this story unsettles people.
Because it forces every believer to confront the difference between image and intimacy.
Between using Jesus and actually following Him.
The world does not need more Christians pretending to be perfect.
It needs surrendered believers who truly know Christ.
People who pray when nobody is watching.
People who obey even when obedience costs them everything.
People who are broken enough to admit they need grace daily.
The Sons of Sceva wanted authority without surrender.
But Jesus still offers something better.
“For whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
The Greek word for “call upon” is:
“To invoke personally.” “To appeal to with dependence.” “To cry out toward.”
The beauty of the Gospel is this:
Jesus does not reject broken people.
But He cannot be reduced into a religious accessory.
There are readers carrying secret fear right now.
Fear that their faith has become routine.
Fear that they know church better than they know Christ.
The fact that this unsettles your spirit may itself be evidence that God is still calling you closer.
And maybe tonight is the night somebody finally stops pretending.
Maybe this is the moment somebody closes the hidden tabs.
Because one day every platform fades.
And the only thing that will matter is whether we truly knew Christ...
and whether He truly knew us.
One of the most dangerous things a person can lose is the difference between sounding close to Jesus and actually knowing Him.
Ang Hindi Naikukuwentong Katotohanan sa Likod ng mga Anak ni Sceva na Sinubukang Gamitin ang Pangalan ni Jesus
May mga taong binabanggit ang pangalan ni Jesus habang umiiyak.
At may mga taong ginagamit ito na parang password.
Ang isa ay nagdadala ng buhay na walang hanggan.
Ang isa naman ay nauuwi sa pagkakalantad.
Maraming Kristiyano ang alam ang kuwento tungkol sa mga Anak ni Sceva sa Gawa 19.
Pero kakaunti lang ang totoong nakakaunawa kung gaano ito kabigat, kabangis, at gaano ito kaakma sa panahon natin ngayon.
Dahil ang kuwentong ito ay hindi lang tungkol sa pitong lalaking Hudyo na nagtangkang magpalayas ng demonyo.
Ito ay kuwento ng mga taong gustong hiramin ang awtoridad ni Jesus nang hindi hinahanap ang relasyon kay Jesus.
Kuwento ito ng mga taong gustong gamitin ang pangalan ni Cristo pero ayaw magpasakop kay Cristo.
Kuwento ito ng relihiyosong performance na walang tunay na intimacy sa Diyos.
Marami pa ring gumagawa nito ngayon.
Tahimik ang buong espirituwal na mundo kapag inilalantad ng langit ang pekeng kabanalan.
Ang Ephesus noong panahon ni Pablo ay isa sa pinakamadilim na siyudad sa buong Roman Empire.
Ang Temple of Artemis ay isa sa pinakatanyag na templo noon.
Ang kadiliman doon ay hindi lihim.
At doon dumating si Apostol Pablo.

“At gumawa ang Dios ng mga bukod na himala sa pamamagitan ng mga kamay ni Pablo: Ano pa't ang mga panyo o mga tapis na nanggaling sa kaniyang katawan ay dinadala sa mga may sakit, at nagsialis sa kanila ang mga sakit, at nagsilabas ang masasamang espiritu.”
At doon nagsimulang mapansin ng iba ang kapangyarihan ni Jesus.
May mga taong nakita ang kapangyarihan...
“Datapuwa't ang ilan sa mga Judiong pagala-galang nagpapalayas ng masasamang espiritu ay nagsikap na banggitin ang pangalan ng Panginoong Jesus.”
Ang salitang ginamit sa Greek para sa “nagsikap” ay:
“Mapangahas na pagtatangka.” “Paggalaw nang walang pahintulot.” “Pag-abot sa bagay na hindi ipinagkaloob.”
Dahil marami pa rin ang gumagawa niyan ngayon.
May mga taong marunong magsuot ng krus pero ayaw mamatay sa kasalanan.
May mga taong marunong mag-quote ng Bible verses pero ayaw magsisi.
May mga taong alam ang Christian language pero hindi kilala ang Diyos sa lihim.
May mga taong mahusay sa church culture pero hindi marunong manalangin.
May mga pulpito na puno ng charisma pero walang consecration.
May mga content creator na habol ay influence, hindi holiness.
At sa kailaliman ng puso nila...
natatakot silang baka natuto na lang silang magmukhang spiritual nang hindi talaga nababago.
Hindi atheist ang mga Anak ni Sceva.
Ang ama nilang si Sceva ay tinawag na:
Pero malayo sila sa tunay na awtoridad ng Diyos.
Dahil ang relihiyong walang relasyon kay Cristo ay walang tunay na kapangyarihan.
Lumapit sila sa lalaking sinasaniban ng demonyo at sinabi:
“Iniutos namin sa iyo sa pangalan ni Jesus na ipinangangaral ni Pablo.”
At agad itong nakilala ng impiyerno.
“At sumagot ang masamang espiritu at sinabi sa kanila, Nakikilala ko si Jesus, at kilala ko si Pablo; datapuwa't sino kayo?”
“Kilala dahil sa awtoridad.” “Kilalang may espirituwal na reputasyon.”
Pero pagdating sa mga Anak ni Sceva?
Sinabi sa Gawa 19:16 na sinugod sila ng lalaking sinasaniban ng demonyo.
At tumakas silang hubad at sugatan.
Dahil ang pekeng espirituwalidad ay laging nauuwi sa pagkakalantad.
Dahil sa panahon natin ngayon, madaling bumili ng platform.
Pero hindi natitinag ang kadiliman sa aesthetics.
Ang tunay na awtoridad ay nanggagaling sa:
Maraming tao ngayon ang pagod na pagod.
Dahil sinusubukan nilang dalhin ang image ng pagiging Kristiyano habang gutom na gutom ang kaluluwa nila.
Marunong silang mag-post tungkol kay Jesus.
Pero hindi sila gumugugol ng oras kasama Siya.
Marunong silang magsalita tungkol sa grace.
Pero tumatakbo sila palayo sa conviction.
Marunong silang sumamba sa harap ng tao.
At unti-unting bumibigay ang kaluluwa sa bigat ng pagpapanggap.
Ito ang dahilan kung bakit mahalaga ang kuwento.
Hindi dahil gusto ng Diyos na ipahiya ang tao.
Kundi dahil ayaw ni Jesus na tratuhin Siya bilang espirituwal na formula.
Noong unang siglo, maraming exorcist ang naniniwalang may supernatural na kapangyarihan ang ilang pangalan.
Ginagamit nila ang pangalan ng mga diyos, anghel, at espiritu bilang parang magical incantation.
At ganoon din ang ginawa ng mga Anak ni Sceva kay Jesus.
Ang pangalan Niya ay konektado sa Kanyang pagkatao.
“Kaya naman siya'y totoong itinaas ng Dios, at binigyan siya ng pangalang lalo sa lahat ng pangalan.”
Sa pag-iisip ng Biblia, ang pangalan ay hindi lang titulo.
Kaya imposibleng gamitin ang pangalan ni Jesus habang tinatanggihan ang pamumuno ni Jesus sa buhay.
At dito tinatamaan ang maraming tao.
Dahil maraming Kristiyano ang tahimik na disconnected sa Diyos.
May mga nagsisimba pero walang tunay na surrender.
May mga umaasa lang sa pananampalataya ng magulang nila.
May mga nabubuhay na lang sa lumang encounter.
At sa ilalim ng lahat ng ito ay isang tanong:
Kilala ba talaga ako ni Jesus?

“Marami ang magsasabi sa akin sa araw na yaon, Panginoon, Panginoon, hindi baga nagsipanghula kami sa iyong pangalan?... At kung magkagayo'y ipahahayag ko sa kanila, Kailan ma'y hindi ko kayo nangakilala.”
Ito ang sumisira sa maling akala na sapat na ang religious activity para masabing transformed.
Hindi kailanman humanga ang Diyos sa performance na walang surrender.
Hindi nagtapos sa kadiliman ang kuwento.
Dahil matapos ang pangyayaring iyon, nagkaroon ng malaking revival sa Ephesus.
Sinunog nila ang kanilang mga aklat ng mahika.
“At tinipon nila ang kanilang mga aklat, at sinunog sa paningin ng lahat.”
Napakamahal ng halaga ng mga iyon.
Kapag totoong gumalaw ang kabanalan ng Diyos, may mga bagay na hindi na maaaring manatili.
Ang salitang Greek para sa “nagpahayag” sa Gawa 19:18 ay:
Nang tumigil ang mga tao sa pagtatago.
At baka iyon din ang dahilan kung bakit tumatama nang malalim ang kuwentong ito.
Dahil pinipilit tayong harapin ang tanong:
O tunay ba natin Siyang sinusundan?
Hindi kailangan ng mundo ng mas marami pang taong magaling magpanggap.
Kailangan nito ng mga totoong surrendered kay Cristo.
Mga taong nananalangin kahit walang nakakakita.
Mga taong nanginginig sa Salita ng Diyos.
Mga taong handang sumunod kahit masakit.
Mga taong alam na araw-araw nilang kailangan ang biyaya ni Jesus.
Gusto ng mga Anak ni Sceva ang kapangyarihan nang walang pagsuko.
Pero may mas mabuting alok si Jesus.
“Sapagka't ang lahat na nagsisitawag sa pangalan ng Panginoon ay mangaliligtas.”
Ang kagandahan ng Ebanghelyo ay ito:
Hindi itinataboy ni Jesus ang mga wasak.
Ang tinatanggihan Niya ay ang maskara.
Pero hindi Siya maaaring gawing accessory lang ng relihiyon.
May mga taong nagbabasa nito ngayon na lihim na pagod.
Pagod magmukhang malapit sa Diyos habang unti-unting lumalamig.
Pero ang conviction ay hindi condemnation.
Baka ang bigat na nararamdaman mo habang binabasa ito ay patunay na tinatawag ka pa rin ng Diyos palapit.
Gusto ng kaaway na manatili kang nakatago.
Gusto ni Jesus na gumaling ka.
ito na ang sandali para tumigil sa pagpapanggap.
Baka oras na para iwan ang lihim na kasalanan.
Baka oras na para bumalik sa panalangin.
Dahil darating ang araw na mawawala ang lahat ng platform.
At ang pinakamahalagang tanong na lang ay:
Nakilala ba talaga natin si Cristo?
Isa sa pinaka-mapanganib na bagay na maaaring mawala sa isang tao ay ang kakayahang makita ang pagkakaiba ng pagiging malapit pakinggan kay Jesus at tunay na pagkakilala kay Jesus.
